task.title: Configure identity provider (IdP) integration for OIDC
task.shortdesc: You must provide information about your identity provider when you use OpenID Connect authentication. Gather information about your identity provider before you begin IdP integration for OIDC.

ul.li: Confirm you are logged in to the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console as an Organization Administrator and have started the IdP integration.

prereq.p: The following information is required to complete IdP integration for OIDC.

ul.li: Issuer: Issuer information for your IdP. A URL for your IdP tokens.
Client ID: The IdP Client ID verifies user identities and provides the information to other services.

Client Secret: A client secret is a random string known only to the OAuth application and the authorization server.
The following characters are not allowed in the client secret. Inspect the client secret and create a new one if any disallowed character is in the secret. \ $ ^ [ ] ' " > <
Authorization URL: The endpoint for the API provider authorization server, to retrieve the authorization code.
Token URL: The URL for the authentication server of the provider, to exchange an authorization code for an access token.
JWKS URL: The URL of JSON Web Key Set for your provider.
Service provider OpenID Configuration URL: The OpenID Connect configuration URL contains the configuration details for the sso.redhat.com OIDC setup.
Redirect URL: The service provider redirect URL, also known as a redirect URL or reply URL, is where your identity provider will redirect users to authenticate to Red Hat.

step.cmd: On the Identity Provider Integration page, click OpenID Connect. The OIDC identity provider configuration form appears.
Using the information you have gathered, fill out the form.

The URLs required for identity provider configuration are provided by Red Hat and are required by your internal identity provider. Copy the URLs and enter them appropriately in your identity provider.
After you verify the information is complete for your identity provider integration, click Create OIDC identity provider integration. A page appears that shows you the configuration information.

info.note: If any information is missing or wrong, update the form and resubmit.

step.cmd: Click Test and enable to complete the identity provider integration. This opens a new window for you to enter your login ID and password.

info.note: Make sure pop-ups are enabled in your browser.

step.cmd: On a successful test, click the Enable button to enable for your organization. If you choose not to enable, you must retest.
